title: protectorflow-circuit-limiters-and-slo-routing-for-safe-batch-cache-tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight runtime protection layer (ProtectorFlow) that applies circuit-style limiters and SLO-aware routing when automated batching/cache tuning proposals are applied. This ticket covers the controller, safe-apply orchestration, anomaly detection hooks, and a rollback playbook so optimization runs cannot violate latency/throughput SLOs for critical routes.
background: Redwood Optimize generates batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations to cut per-token unit cost. Past experiments showed 2–3x cost improvement on tail workloads, but a small fraction of routes experienced SLO regressions during aggressive tuning. We need an automated safety layer that can: (1) enforce per-route latency/throughput limiters, (2) dynamically route traffic to conservative model variants or uncached paths on anomalies, and (3) safely roll back config changes with minimal request loss.
scope:
- Implement ProtectorFlow controller as a sidecar/agent in the runtime orchestration path.
- Create limiters: concurrency, per-tenant qps, token-rate ceilings, and burst windows.
- SLO-aware routing decisions based on real-time latency percentiles and per-route throughput.
- Integrate anomaly detector (metrics+SLO thresholds + simple ML detector) to trigger immediate rollback or routing shifts.
- Safe-apply orchestration: gradual canary apply with automated checkpoints and quick rollback actions.
- Add observability (dashboard tiles, audit log entries, and incident hooks).
design_notes:
- Limiters are implemented as resource descriptors separate from tuning proposals so they can be updated independently.
- SLO signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, request success rate, queue depth, and token per-second throughput. Use exponentially weighted moving averages for smoothing.
- Routing fallback: route to legacy (uncached, lower-batched) variant or alternate region with spare capacity.
- Anomaly detection initial iteration uses z-score on p95 and sliding-window spike detection; future iterations will use lightweight classifiers trained on historical rollout data.
- All control ops include an immutable audit record with proposer id and commit sha for traceability.
acceptance_criteria:
- ProtectorFlow deploys to runtime staging with limiters enabled.
- Automated tuning run triggers canary apply and ProtectorFlow enforces configured concurrency and token-rate ceilings.
- When injected latency spikes cross defined thresholds, traffic is routed to fallback within 30s and the canary is rolled back automatically.
- Dashboard shows limiter state, active fallbacks, and recent rollbacks.
- End-to-end test simulating 40% increased tail latency validates rollback and zero data leak in audit logs.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy ProtectorFlow agent to staging runtime nodes.
2) Run synthetic workload with controlled latency injection and validate limiter behavior.
3) Enable on low-traffic customer bucket in pre-prod and monitor for 48h.
4) Progressive enablement: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% of automated tuning runs over two weeks, with manual gate at 50%.
5) Post-rollout review and performance tuning for limiter thresholds.
monitoring_playbook:
- Primary alerts: p95 > SLO*1.3 after tuning apply; controller rollback executed.
- Secondary alerts: sustained queue depth increase > 60s, error-rate > 1%.
- On alert: on-call inspects ProtectorFlow audit log, checks canary id, and verifies fallback routing was applied.
- If rollback didn't trigger: execute manual rollback and escalate to runtime on-call.
- Post-incident: record in incident board and attach tuning proposal id for RCA.
rollback_steps:
1) ProtectorFlow automated rollback will revert batching/cache config to last-known-good and route traffic back to primary variant.
2) If automation fails, run 'pf rollback <canary-id>' CLI to revert configs and drain new connections.
3) Notify impacted teams and create postmortem if customer-facing SLOs were violated.
4) Tag problematic tuning proposal to be excluded from future auto-suggestions until reviewed.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for limiter rules, routing decision matrix, and audit logging.
- Integration tests: run end-to-end apply/rollback in CI with synthetic latency profiles.
- Chaos test: inject intermittent p95 spikes during canary to ensure fallback and rollback occur under load.
- Load test: ensure overhead of ProtectorFlow agent is <3% CPU and adds <2ms median latency.
security_considerations:
- Audit logs include proposer identity and cryptographic commit reference.
- Access to ProtectorFlow control APIs requires RBAC role 'tuning-controller' and mTLS between controller and runtime.
- Data in logs is redacted for PII and API keys.
- Security review required before GA (see security_review_required flag).
notes: We intentionally keep initial anomaly detector simple to avoid false positives. Thresholds will be tuned from pre-prod telemetry. Consider integrating with Optimize's existing scoring so proposals deemed 'risky' start with more conservative batch/cache defaults.
